gloss: to get into, to slip into

forms.label: Past polite
forms.negative: {入|い}り{込|こ}みませんでした

forms.label: ている past
forms.negative: {入|い}り{込|こ}んでいなかった

forms.label: ている past polite
forms.negative: {入|い}り{込|こ}んでいませんでした

definitions.gloss: to get into, to slip into, to enter deeply
definitions.explanation: To go deep into a place, often suggesting entering somewhere that is enclosed, hidden, or not easily accessible.

definitions.gloss: to become deeply involved, to be absorbed in
definitions.explanation: To become immersed in or deeply engaged with something such as a story, role, or activity.

examples.japanese: {猫|ねこ}が{押|お}し{入|い}れに{入|い}り{込|こ}んだ。
examples.english: The cat got into the closet.

examples.japanese: {雨水|あまみず}が{建物|たてもの}の{中|なか}に{入|い}り{込|こ}んでいた。
examples.english: Rainwater had gotten inside the building.

examples.japanese: {不審者|ふしんしゃ}が{敷地|しきち}{内|ない}に{入|い}り{込|こ}んだ{形跡|けいせき}がある。
examples.english: There are traces of a suspicious person having gotten onto the premises.

examples.japanese: {小説|しょうせつ}の{世界|せかい}に{入|い}り{込|こ}んでしまった。
examples.english: I became completely absorbed in the world of the novel.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{自分|じぶん}の{研究|けんきゅう}に{入|い}り{込|こ}みすぎて、{周|まわ}りが{見|み}えなくなる。
examples.english: He gets so deeply absorbed in his research that he loses sight of his surroundings.

notes:
A compound verb combining {入|はい}る (to enter) and {込|こ}む (into, deeply). The {込|こ}む component adds the nuance of going deep or becoming immersed.

CONJUGATION (godan, む row):
- {入|い}り{込|こ}まない (negative)
- {入|い}り{込|こ}みます (polite)
- {入|い}り{込|こ}んで (te-form)
- {入|い}り{込|こ}んだ (past)

Note that this word also has the reading {入|はい}り{込|こ}む (hairikomu), which is a separate entry. The いりこむ reading tends to suggest slipping in or penetrating, while はいりこむ emphasizes physically entering a space.
